record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Suppose two disjoint Cauchy surfaces in an asymptotically flat vacuum spacetime carry isometric initial data. Must the spacetime be stationary, meaning that it admits a timelike Killing vector field?

artifact.category_tag: Stationarity and Killing fields in vacuum spacetimes
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, $4$-dimensional, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat solution of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$. Recall that a Cauchy surface is a smooth spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ such that every inextendible causal curve in $M$ meets $\Sigma$ exactly once, and the induced Cauchy data on $\Sigma$ consists of the pair $(h,K)$ where $h$ is the Riemannian metric induced on $\Sigma$ and $K$ is the second fundamental form of $\Sigma$ in $(M,g)$. Two Cauchy data sets $(\Sigma_1,h_1,K_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,h_2,K_2)$ are called isometric if there exists a diffeomorphism $\phi:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$ with $\phi^*h_2=h_1$ and $\phi^*K_2=K_1$. The spacetime $(M,g)$ is said to be stationary if it admits a smooth Killing vector field that is timelike in the asymptotic region.

Question: Suppose $(M,g)$ admits two disjoint Cauchy surfaces $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ whose induced vacuum Cauchy data $(\Sigma_1,h_1,K_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,h_2,K_2)$ are isometric. Must $(M,g)$ be stationary, i.e., must it admit a Killing vector field that is timelike at infinity?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as an open question in mathematical relativity. Searches on standard sources (arXiv, surveys on open problems in general relativity) do not turn up a proof or counterexample for the general asymptotically flat vacuum case; partial results exist only under strong additional hypotheses. No conclusive resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Initial Data for the Cauchy Problem in General Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes describing Cauchy data and open questions about uniqueness and symmetry in vacuum spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference confirming the Cauchy problem framework in which the question is posed; no resolution of the stated problem is indicated.

status_evidence.title: Existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of splitting/rigidity results in globally hyperbolic spacetimes and remaining open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Related rigidity/splitting problems are noted as open, supporting that the stated stationarity-from-repeated-data question remains open.
